p.i: frigidæ fumentisq; est natura, quam ob causam adjungunt cepas, ut harum acrimoniâ gulam, irritet.

Cauliculi sale & aceto condiuntur, inque cibos[?] hiemales astiuosq; reseruantur, aquâ deinde calidâ abluuntur aut vino, ut salsugo & acrimonia contracta ex conditura hebetetur, abluti oleo superimfuso apponuntur.

In horum olerum censu sunt mercuria-lis, asparagus, malua, rumex, buglossa, quae in-re cibaria non postremam dignitatem atque autoritatem reportauit; propterea quod in vi-hum[?] conjecta[?] potantibus[?] animi hilaritatem cre-at melancoliam, pellit.

Verum in hac & similibus peculiariter ac privatim naturam, ac vim singulorum considerari oportet, quatenus videl. vel sedulâ curâ excoluntur, vel certis ac receptis experimen-tis salutaria & utilia hominum vitae observata sunt.
Herbarum enim in cibis alia placent, saepe[?] alia folio, alia radice, nonnulla flore, quadam cymis, hoc est, tenerioribus caulicu-lis; aliqua capite & summitati-bus, &c.

page.notes: The whole page is in italic type. Doubtful readings are marked [?]: the first letters of "cibos" (printed as eibos), the word before "vi-" on the line break, "conjecta", "potantibus", "saepe" (printed with a ligature that is hard to read), and the page number 175, which is partly obscured. Line-end hyphens follow the printed hyphens. Long s is written as s throughout, and "&" is escaped as & for XML. The "§ 2" at the foot is treated as the signature and "CAP." as the catchword.
